notes.html: Astralagus: herb of creativity. Helps bridge any gap there might be between the thought and the creation of the reality.

Willpower, Desire, Creation, Manifestation

The magician is the representation of pure willpower. She takes all that is available to her and moulds and transforms it to her desires. With her hand pointing to the ground and her wand pointing to the sky, she is the manifestation of the ancient phrase "As above so below" - meaning that earth reflects heaven, what is within is also without, the microcosm is the macrocosm. Naturally, this phrase is the origin of what is commonly understood as magic.

Manifesting, co-creation, will, ability, focusing, miracles, intentions, potential, power, masculine active principle.

The Magician represents our birthright ability to create our own reality. It symbolises our will to achieve our heart's desire. It is our power to manifest through deliberate focus and unbreakable faith. In readings, it signals the potential to manifest now, provided that there is full trust, commitment and inspired action.

Bold, Self-Determined, Skilled  

A giant of a man stands and manipulates a figure between his fingers. His translucent silhouette and enormous moon ruling the background suggest the realm of the inner landscape, but his uncompromising presence dispels the mystery and replaces it with sheer force of will. He has mastered his subconscious, and as a result, the material world around him.

The Magician is bold with his decisive power. He is self-determined and self-confident, and possesses a vision he truly believes should be realized. He is passionate, creative, and above all deeply connected to his surroundings, to his vision, to his life. When you receive this card, expect to receive a bolt of energy: what you are doing is worthwhile, and you have the means within you to accomplish it. This is not a time for doubt, but for action.

inspiration • enthusiasm • potential

A vent bursts open on the riverbank and a pillar of flame rushes out. One fiery tendril loops crazily around the blazing column, finally unfurling to capture the Page of Wands. Cast up into the air, he is drawn inward toward the ethereal fire. A nubile conduit, he courses with the energy of the inferno. A power kindles in his spirit and he feels the call to begin something magical. 

When you see the Page of Wands in a reading, you are about to set out on a journey of the mind. You have been struck with some novel or wonderful idea, and you have the naive, unfettered enthusiasm of a child to catalyze it. Take risks like you’ve never been hurt. Believe wholeheartedly in something. Your divine vibrancy will bring your vision to life. Your courage and passion will see it to completion.
Justice suggests that the choices you make now will have consequences in the future, and that you will ultimately be held accountable for your actions.

Keeping balance without being impatient


Often associated with balance, moderation, and harmony, Temperance can be a reminder to find a middle ground and avoid extremes in your life. It's also a sign to trust the process and have faith that everything will work out in the end.

Often associated with passion, energy, and adventure. He is a fearless and ambitious individual who is always seeking new experiences and challenges. This card can be a sign that you may need to tap into your own sense of adventure and take risks to achieve your goals. The Knight of Wands is also a reminder to stay focused and determined, and to be confident in your own abilities.
Feeling creatively stifled, not able to pursue your ambitions, not able to live out their true purpose” ()
Reflection, Contemplation, Inner work

The Star brings renewed hope and faith, and a sense that you are truly blessed by the Universe. You are entering a peaceful, loving phase in your life, filled with calm energy, mental stability and more in-depth understanding of both yourself and others around you.

With The Star card, anything is possible and the magic is flowing around you. Your heart is full of hope, and your soul is being uplifted to the highest of highs as you realize that your dreams really can come true.
Fairness · Truth · Balance · Accountability · Cause and effect · Integrity · Decisions · Karma
Completion · Integration · Achievement · Fulfilment · Wholeness · Harmony · Advancement · Belonging

Self-knowledge,  intuition


The High Priestess, like the moon, sees through the darkness, illuminating what is hidden, reminding us that all we need to know is already within us.

It is related, numerologically, to the Eights of the Minor Arcana, and to Strength: cards which speak to self-knowledge, self-acceptance, and moments when you are able to look within yourself, draw upon your power, and move forwards.
This card creates space to ask – gently – about the difference between what someone chooses to reveal, and the whole truth of the matter.
Inspiration · Creation · New projects · Potential · Enthusiasm · Desire · Willpower · Energy  ·  Growth (represented by the shoots on the wand)

What we can call the 'negative imagination' makes us look at everything as worthless or boring. There seems to be nothing worth getting up for, nothing worth doing, and nothing worth examining. The three cups symbolize the person's past experience. Bored by what life has given him he does not recognize the new opportunities being offered to him by the fourth cup. The resemblance of that cup to the Ace suggests that the new possibilities can lead to happiness and satisfaction. In the main, however, the card shows a situation when everything in life has come to appear the same. The card sometimes shows apathy resulting from a dull, unstimulating environment.
notes.source: Seventy-Eight Degrees of Wisdom by Rachel Pollack

The Empress represents fertility, creativity, and growth. She is a powerful symbol of feminine energy. She represents the mother archetype and embodies nurturing, support, and unconditional love. She is associated with growth, creativity, and abundance, and encourages us to connect with our intuition and follow our passions.
Abundance, Nurturing, Fertility, Feminine Energy Manifested, Creation, Sensuality, In tune with the body, Maternal warmth

Messengers, child-like, somewhat impatient, hasty, spontaneous. Represent curiosity, possibilities, youthful energy.

Metamorphosis · Endings · Rebirth · Transformation · Transition · Tumultuous time · Acceptance · Letting go · Time to move on · Closing one door to open another · Going through what cannot be avoided · Release
Elder: Herb of Purification. "Helps the death of the old to be transmuted into the new rebirthed self. It acts as a guardian spirit during the metamorphosis and brings ease as the transition occurs.”

Hawthorn - helps to release feelings of disharmony. It reinstates inner calm and poise after a period of conflict and struggle. The heart chakra will be fortified and a greater sense of ease and self-love will be renewed.

The Ten of Swords is often seen as a painful ending, betrayal, or a difficult situation that has come to an abrupt and final end. It can be a difficult card to receive, but it can also be a sign that you're ready to move on from a situation that is no longer serving you. It's important to take the time to process your feelings and allow yourself to grieve the end of this situation.

After a period of pause and reflection with the Hanged Man, the Death card symbolises the end of a major phase or aspect of your life that you realise is no longer serving you, opening up the possibility of something far more valuable and essential.

It represents our ability to transform ourselves and rise from the ashes of our old ways. It's the symbolic death of all that does not serve us anymore, and the rebirth into a new self. It's the beautiful transition out of the chrysalis, leaving the goo behind. In readings, it signals a moment of transmutation, where that which is not needed falls away, allowing for the transition into a new state. It's something that ends in order to make room for something greater.

fixated on money • growing dependent • losing meaning 

A blood red Knight sits immured in his armor, glittering Pentacle propped up as a shield. He peers out from his helmet, eyes narrowed, looking for danger. But for all his awareness, he seems totally oblivious to the fact that his steed is the legendary unicorn, nuzzling dispiritedly among the strawberries. The Knight’s bare feet also belie his lackluster attention to detail. When a true calamity does befall him, he will be woefully under-prepared. 

 The Knight is a conflicted creature. Having attained no small degree of success, he grows dependent on the tokens that have carried him safely thus far. He no longer sees their interconnected beauty; merely their utility. He is fixated on furthering his causes. If you pull this Knight in a reading, know that you may need to back off a little. Take a broader view. Appreciate the magic that makes your lifestyle possible. Otherwise, you will face a Pyrrhic victory devoid of meaning or gratification

Material reward • new adventure • abundance

Ensconced in a sturdy brick wall, a wooden door swings open, bearing the sign of the Pentacle. Beyond it lie many mysteries, but a few gnarled trees suggest an orchard, laden with fruit, smelling richly of loam. Light and bubbles stream out, beckoning the reader in. Dare to cross the threshold. Immerse yourself in wonder. 

 When you see a tantalizing opportunity, take it. This card promises great material reward for projects undertaken, particularly if they’re something novel or unexplored. Though you may not be able to see over the wall and divine what you are truly choosing, dare to take the road less traveled. You may find that it pays off in the long run. Rise up to the challenge and begin your new adventure.

• Don’t resist necessary endings, 
  • Break bad habits or patterns of behaviour
  • Let go of unhealthy attachments. Purge the old belongings, memories and baggage that are getting in your way.
Queens: Feminine energy, nurturing and compassionate

Yellow Dock - “ helps to free inner reserves of strength and fortitude. For those afraid of change and stuck in old conditions, it will help clear out some of the old sludge and rebuild a stronger inner self who is not afraid of dancing with life,”
Valerian: helps relieve self-judgment and may be used for self-purification when one is feeling the “guilties.” Helps one to “feel warmer” toward the self.
Swords Court cards: When a figure's head is above the clouds — seeing through situations/deceit clearly. Or, head in the clouds (reverse: unable to come down to earth).

balancing work • productive • priorities 

A young man sits atop the brick wall, above it all, tossing his two Pentacles with practiced ease. He keeps those opposing forces in balance, cocking an eyebrow as one falls back into his open palm. His cap at a jaunty angle, a playful smile on his lips, he exudes the effortless confidence of a man who seems to have everything under control.

Life’s imbalance is its greatest strength. To the man that masters the back and forth motion, the perpetual movement propels him into a steady, productive rhythm. Keep it all together by not paying too much attention to one thing. Accept that everything has its time and its place, and it is up to you to decide when it’s time to move onwards.

determination • intellectual power

A winged sword is driven into the snow, as if fallen from the hand of God. Like all the Aces, it radiates power and energy. The bird on its hilt scowls with incisive intensity. The center-most eye, glaring panopticon, sees all. ~ upright meaning: mental clarity  

The Ace of Swords cleaves through indecision and deceit. It is the mental clarity that comes with keen intelligence. It may indicate an epiphany. When you pull this card, you may be driven with a determination borne of ruthlessness. Examine your motivations and ensure you’re not being too tyrannical. Master the sword, and wield its mighty power for good.

New beginnings, a leap of faith, enthusiasm, innocence, living in the moment.

The Fool represents our soul's innocence as it dives into the physical world. Much like the jester in medieval times, the Fool is fun, spontaneous, energetic and eager for what's ahead. In readings, it signals new beginnings and reminds us to trust that life is good and worth the journey.

Intuition, inner guidance, stillness, insight, voice within, meditation, being receptive to listen, feminine passive principle.

The High Priestess represents our own inner guidance, the voice of wisdom guarded in the unconscious, that wise voice within we can all tune into for help. Our ability to receive insight from other realms. The feminine receptive principle which can be expressed through silence, stillness,meditation and receptivity. In readings it signals the invitation to look deeper, to get in touch with our Inner self, to listen to our intuition. It indicates your intuition is trying to guide you and you are being invited to listen to your instincts.

Abundance, feeling rich, in tune with the body, nurturing a new project, pregnancy, fertility, unity, feminine energy manifested, creation.

The Empress represents our ability to conceive, nurture and birth healthy projects. It reminds us of our connection with the energy of abundance available in the Universe, in nature and inside ourselves. It invites us to feel rich and to allow the energy of prosperity and wellness to flow through us so that our projects can come to fruition with ease in the physical world. Letting go of any worries and fears, know your worth. In readings, it signals material reward, as long as we can allow it through self-care, receptivity, trust, joy and openness. It can also point to pregnancy.

Bossing up, determination, action, planning, strategy, taking charge, leadership, logic


The Emperor represents our determination, self-confidence, command and ability to make things happen. It's bossing up and doing what it takes. In readings it signals the need to take disciplinary actions, organization and strategy put into practice, being determined towards reaching a specific goal. It's about standing up and taking charge.

Spiritual teachings, finding a mentor/guru, establishing a belief system, commitment, marriage

The Hierophant represents our initial need to develop a belief system that assists with making sense of the mysteries of life. It's seeking for a mentor or a guide, often on spiritual matters, religion or the occult. It involves all the processes of learning, studying, and adopting fixed beliefs, habits and rituals. In readings, it signals learning with experts or knowledgeable teachers, taking courses and learning processes that help with the beginning of the spiritual journey, before turning within for answers. It can also signal an important commitment or marriage.

Choice, polarity, duality, a deep spiritual love connection, twin flames, union


The Lovers represents our urge for connection. It speaks to love and sex and all kinds of exchange with other selves. It is the pull to share experiences while making the choice between knowing we're all One, and thus abundant, secure, free and worthy of endless love in all its forms; or believing we're separate and alone, and thus giving in to energies of fear, lack, manipulation and control. In readings, it signals the potential for experiencing a deep fulfilling connection and expanding through it,or the presence of such  a connection.

Movement forward, determination, pursuing goals, self-confidence

The Chariot represents our determination to succeed, our movement towards victory. It speaks to pushing towards our goals letting nothing distract us. It's concentration of energy, sustained effort that is fueled by a healthy sense of ego: ""I know who I am and what I want, and I will do it"". In readings, it signals a strong energy of emotionally-driven movement which, ideally, is not brutal, but firm and direct. It's the discipline, confidence, grit and emotional motivation necessary to succeed.

Embracing shadow, courage, calmness, self-compassion, acceptance, enduring with grace, mastering raw emotions

Strength represents our ability to face challenges with acceptance and grace. It's neither resisting nor trying to hide or escape from our shadow self as projected onto others. It's knowing the external world reflects our internal world, and thus choosing to master one's raw emotions instead of reacting with anger or explosive behavior. In readings it signals an invitation to remain strong and graceful in the face of adversity, to embrace the present with openness, kindness, compassion and acceptance of self and others. It also indicates confidence and inner strength.

Needing to be alone, focusing inward, looking for answers within, seeking greater understanding, mentor/guide

The Hermit represents our need to withdraw from the world in order to seek for answers within. It's a moment of introspection, focusing inward, a desire for stillness and a deep longing for answers and a greater understanding. In readings it signals the need for a personal retreat, it's a seeking for the knowledge that comes from within, it means someone is being guided to look within rather than out for clarity and the truth.

Changes, fate, luck, divine intervention, a sense of destiny, a turn of events, natural laws

Wheel of Fortune represents our growing realization of the mysteries of the Universe. It's knowing there are natural laws at work in the cosmos of which we have no control. It represents the inevitable changes which are always for the best. It's a sense of order and movement, of fate and flow. In readings it signals the wheels of change turning in our favour, it's an invitation to trust everything is always working out for us, it's surrendering and being receptive to change.

Fairness, balance, being impartial, decision, karma, cause and effect, taking responsibility

Justice represents our recognition that we reap what we sow. It speaks to taking responsibility for our actions, knowing and accepting the results we create. It recommends being fair, honest, ethical and righteous, so that one plants only the right seeds. In readings, it signals the result of a past choice. It's karma being balanced. It can also indicate an invitation to recognize one's distortions and make amends. Or it might simply point to a confirmation that you deserve all the good things being presented to you, for they simply reflect your harmonious past decisions."

Surrender, letting go, pause, reflection, new perspective, suspending action,acceptance

The Hanged man represents a necessary pause in order to reflect upon a situation, ideally seeking for a new perspective on it. It requires surrendering control of what is, with acceptance and openness. In readings,  it signals a moment of apparent stagnation, in which the temporary lack of movement is supposed to encourage learning to let go, practicing patience, giving up urgency, being open to new perspectives, an invitation to see things from a new angle, an opportunity to change one's mind.

The Death
Transformation, rebirth, transmutation, transition, initiation, rising from the ashes

The Death card represents our ability to transform ourselves and rise from the ashes of our old ways. It's the symbolic death of all that does not serve us anymore, and the rebirth into a new self. It's the beautiful transition out of the chrysalis, leaving the goo behind. In readings, it signals a moment of transmutation, where that which is not needed falls away, allowing for the transition into a new state. It's something that ends in order to make room for something greater.

Emotional regulation, inner harmony, moderation, patience, healing and integration, balance

The Temperance card represents our need to regroup and process our process, thoughts and feelings. It's an invitation to center the self in order to distil and integrate experiences. A moment of emotional regulation that leads to balance and good health in all areas - physical, emotional and mental. The promise of vitality and well-being. It readings it signals the potential for achieving inner harmony through moderation. It's distilling and integrating, breathing with one's emotions, feeling centered, balanced and whole.

Restriction, fear, control, manipulation, illusion, separation, deception, addiction

The Devil represents our disconnection from the truth of who we are: worthy, free, divine and whole. It's the getting lost in the illusions of separation and fear that leads to all sorts of unhealthy dynamics, addiction, restrictions, deception, and the need to manipulate and control in order to succeed or feel loved. In readings, it signals the potential to releasenfear and choose love. It's an opportunity to free oneself from the false mental narratives of lack, abandonment, separation and despair. It's an invitation to choose to experience love, oneness and freedom instead.

Upheaval, sudden changes, unexpected detours, chaos, crisis, things falling apart

The Tower represents the collapse of structures which hadn't been built on solid foundations. It's a necessary and often uncomfortable, quick and explosive disruption which aims to bring significant change to a situation that can no longer remain the same. In readings,  it signals sudden dramatic upheavals, detours or crisis that often provide a much overdue wake-up call, and the preparation for a rebuilding based on love and truth.

Healing after deep trauma, hope renewed, dream come true, faith, wish fulfillment

The Star represents the calm after the storm. It's that feeling of hope renewed and deep healing that happens after profound trauma has been released. In readings, it signals the potential for deep healing that leads to regaining motivation, it's faith being restored, it's feeling hopeful and serene, it's wish fulfilment, the light at the end of the tunnel, and the renovated promise of dreams coming true. It's a reset, a restart.

The unknown, the  unconscious, emotional  wounds, hidden cause,  mystery, uncertainty

The Moon represents all of that which is hidden from the conscious mind. From the root o four emotional wounds to the unknown basis of our connections. It harbours our fears, traumas, and our shadow self. It sheds light through our inner darkness. In readings, it signals an opportunity to dive deeper into ourselves and see the truth of what's  actually moving us. It's an invitation to reveal what's hidden behind our fears and anxieties. It's the potential to bring clarity to a situation which is currently confusing and unclear.

Joy, happiness, success, inspiration, realization, positivity, radiance

The Sun represents experiencing absolute joy, bursting with enthusiasm and positivity. It's about feeling invigorated and inspired, expansive and free. It's the achievement of success and dreams come true. It personifies happiness in all areas of an individual's life. In readings, it signals a period of utter bliss where one feels radiantly energized, confident and absolutely worthy of all the glory and blessings coming their way. It brings a feeling of optimism and fulfilment, a time to shine one's brightest light."

Judgment
Spiritual calling, true vocation, self-reflection, awakening, finding one's essence, bringing something back

Judgment represents an awakening to one's true calling in life. It's the heart's calling, an urge to find one's own essence. It's about recognizing and pursuing one's true vocation. In readings, it signals the potential to awaken to new possibilities in life. It often feels like a deep call for a change. It's listening to our heart's desire and the inspired action that follows. It's the angels calling for the cleansing of all guilts and burdens that keep us stuck in life, and the pursuing the truth of our real contribution to the world. It's a call for the courage to be who you really are. It can also indicate the return of something/someone important.

Graduation, completion, end of a cycle, next level, integration, advancement, accomplishment

The World card represents the realization of an important goal, the reaching the end of the race, the graduation with honour, and reaping the rewards of a successful journey. In readings, it signals the end of a successful journey and the feelings of satisfaction and contentment it brings. It is a positive sign of personal fulfilment and accomplishment that foresees further advancement and explores new ways to contribute to the world. It indicates the end of a cycle, it says ""Congratulations, you've made it! What's next?

Love

When it comes to love and relationships, the Death tarot card love meaning can indicate being stuck in emotional dynamics that are no longer working. If you are already in a relationship, for the relationship to continue, you must learn to embrace change. Sometimes, this card can also indicate that you may want to end the relationship, especially if it hasn't been going well. It is important to remember that all doors that close with the Death tarot card open another. While Death may be difficult to accept in a love tarot reading, transformations for one partner or another may be what is needed to help both individuals grow. It is also important to remember that the cards are suggestions, and that you have the choice to either accept and welcome your relationship's transformation, or let it go. While initially scary, the transformations that the Death tarot card can bring to love can also be positive. In less stressful terms, it can be the coming of a new era, such as an engagement. If you are not in a relationship, the Death tarot card love meaning can instead point to beliefs, attitudes or behaviors that you are currently shedding that can help you develop healthier, stronger relationships.

Career

If you’ve been considering a career change, the upright Death card can be a signal that you should take the plunge and act now. You may have been through a period of apathy, disinterest and frustration at your current job, and should you not take decisive action, events in life may force you to make a change. You may be clinging to your current path because it offers stability, certainty and safety, but if you are otherwise unhappy or feeling unchallenged, there is much more to lose than your comfort. Often when one door closes, another one opens; embrace the shifts occurring right now and dive in.

Finances

Loss is signaled by the Death tarot card, meaning that you may unfortunately be dealing with a loss in your financial resources. This period can also be the initiator to a transformation in how you handle your relationship to your money and what you value. The lessons you learn from this time can lead to practical changes when it comes to managing your resources, as well as to spiritual changes in knowing what is truly important to you.

Feelings
The upright Death card signals a powerful moment of transformation and renewal. This person senses that your connection is evolving; they feel the end of old patterns and are open to new possibilities with you. Their emotions run deep as they recognize the need for change and growth within themselves, which can strengthen your bond if nurtured. Your own feelings mirror this shift. The upright Death card reveals that you, too, are experiencing significant personal changes. You may be ready to shed past baggage or emotional ties that no longer serve you. Embrace this transformative energy; it urges you to let go of what holds you back and welcome fresh beginnings in both love and life.

Actions 

When you draw the upright Death card, you’re being asked to embrace transformation and release what no longer serves you. This is a powerful moment for letting go of old habits, relationships, or mindsets that hinder your growth. Consider decluttering your space as a physical manifestation of this change; donate items that hold emotional weight but no longer resonate with who you are becoming. Additionally, reflect on areas in your life where fear may be holding you back. Perhaps it’s time to confront those fears head-on. Engage in new experiences that challenge your comfort zone, allowing yourself to evolve into the person you're meant to be.

- Revel in your success,  Enjoy the praise and recognition you’re getting

- Get ready for the next step  - This is not time to rest on your laurels, once the celebrations are over, prepare for what comes next. Keep it up!

Love

When this card shows up in a love tarot reading, get ready to embark on a new adventure. The Fool tarot meaning in love signals that you'll need to experience new things in order to find the romance that you desire. Be willing to take risks, be bold and expand your vision of the world and you may end up finding love in the most unlikely places. Surprises are in store for you. Since the Fool represents the start of new journeys, it's tarot meaning in love can be an indicator of new relationships. As with any new relationship, you may fear rejection, but this card indicates that this should not hold you back. When you open yourself up to the world, even in the face of embarassment or rejection, you may find what you are looking for. In love and relationships, the Fool tells us that we should be confident and have faith that all things will work out well. It tells us that instead of giving up, we keep trying, and look at the world with innocence and wonder. The Fool tarot meaning in love encourages open-eyed innocence and positivity.

Career

New beginnings are on their way, when the Fool appears in your career tarot reading. If you’ve been looking to start a new career path, change jobs, get a promotion, or even start your own venture, the Fool can be a welcome card to begin your new journey. Even if no new drastic changes are coming your way or planned, this card can feel like a fresh breath of air into old projects. You can be filled with new energy, and new innovative ideas can be put into action now. What is important now is to be very aware of the opportunities that are there, and have the courage to take them when they appear.

Finances

When it comes to finances, you may be in a period where you are feeling spontaneous and idealistic. All spending now can be for the purpose of adventure and exploration. Want to go on a trip? Or learn a new skill? It can be easy for you to fund these purchases now. There can be a feeling that you will have all that you need, so there’s no need to worry about the bills, and more emphasis on feeling expansive and curious.

Feelings

The Fool upright reveals a thrilling sense of excitement and spontaneity in how this person feels about you. They are captivated by your adventurous spirit, seeing endless potential in the unknown journey ahead. A rush of curiosity and hope fills them, as if they’re ready to leap into something new together. Their feelings are fresh, unburdened by past experiences, allowing them to fully embrace the possibilities that await. The arrival of The Fool signals your own desire for freedom and exploration. You feel invigorated at the thought of stepping outside your comfort zone or starting a new chapter in life. An openness stirs within you, craving adventure and urging you to trust your instincts: follow where your heart leads without fear or hesitation.

Actions

When you draw The Fool upright, you're being asked to embrace spontaneity and adventure. It encourages you to let go of fear and take a leap into the unknown, suggesting that now is the time for exploration and new experiences. Consider trying something you've always wanted to do but hesitated about; perhaps signing up for a class or traveling somewhere unfamiliar. This card also urges you to adopt a fresh perspective; view challenges as opportunities rather than obstacles. Allow yourself to be playful and curious, engaging with life in an open-hearted way. Trust your instincts, take risks, and enjoy the journey ahead without overthinking it.

profound change • new chapter • renewal

Skeletal fingers reach out, closing around an evanescent rose. The border between the flower and its surroundings seems to blur, and delicate petals disintegrate into the breeze. The Grim has come to take his own.

This can be a frightening card to receive at first. Loss and change are inevitable and often quite painful. Brace yourself to shed something that seems integral to your life. But inevitably, out of its remains will grow something more beautiful and more adapted to your needs than you could have anticipated. Pulling the card of Death is just a sign of forthcoming renewal. Though it loses its familiar form, that which passes away only breaks down into simpler components and dissipates out into the universe.

Love

As with its general meaning, the Magician tarot meaning in love indicates making things manifest. Skill, creativity, desire and determination will bring success in love. Should you be searching for love, the Magician suggests you take action and create opportunities to meet someone who you desire. Because the Magician in tarot also represents resourcefulness and skill, it is also still important to make sure that no deception or illusions are at work. For both singles and couples, the Magician brings excitement and a desire to experiment.

Career

There are likely to be opportunities in your midst, and you may be able to harness them if you take decisive action. The Magician is the card of manifestation, meaning should you have the desire and commitment to pursue whatever it is you want in your career, you’re likely to find success. Look behind any successful person, and you’ll likely find intense willpower and drive; this is the root of all ambition. The same goes if you’re looking to start a business; harness that drive, and keep it motivated to manifest your dream career. Sometimes, if this card represents another person, such as a colleague or business partner, you may want to approach with caution, as they may not be everything they appear to be.

Finances

There can be increased financial opportunities available right now, you’ll likely just need to pursue them with gusto. The magician works with many tools to make his will manifest. Try and take a look at the tools you have available; they can be the key for you now. What skills do you have? What abilities are you not putting to use right now? Being creative can yield results.

Feelings

The arrival of The Magician ignites a thrilling sense of excitement and potential in how someone feels about you. This person sees you as a wellspring of inspiration, irresistibly drawn to your energy and charisma. They believe that together, you can create something meaningful and transformative. Their feelings brim with enthusiasm, viewing this connection as an opportunity for growth and manifestation. As for your own emotions, The Magician reveals that you are empowered and ready to take action. You feel confident in your ability to shape reality and influence the situation at hand. This card urges you to tap into your skills and creativity, reminding you that the power to manifest what you desire in this relationship lies within you.

Actions

In the presence of The Magician, you’re encouraged to tap into your unique skills and resources to bring your dreams to life. Embrace a proactive mindset, recognizing that you have the power to create change in your life. Start by setting clear intentions for what you want to achieve, whether it’s a personal project or a career goal. Take tangible steps like enrolling in a course to enhance your abilities or networking with individuals who inspire you. Additionally, practice visualization techniques daily; see yourself succeeding and feel the emotions associated with that success. This is your moment! Take action and make things happen.

Love
The High Priestess in a love tarot reading can signal almost imperceptible and unconscious changes in one's emotional state. A calm surface can hide intense emotions, and even seemingly simple dates can turn into raging passions. The High Priestess tarot love meaning suggests that one needs patience, and trust for your intuition. Be honest with others and yourself, and let what is hidden come to the surface. In a relationship, the High Priestess shows increasing intimacy and openness. In a love tarot reading, this card signals that honesty is essential to making your relationship as strong as it can be.

Career
When it comes to your career, the High Priestess may signal a period of education or higher learning. You may be returning to school for training. If you’re in a creative field, this card also can suggest new inspiration coming into your work. When making big choices about your future career or projects, the High Priestess also suggests relying on your gut instincts. There’s likely a lot of information there that will aid you. At times, this card can also signal the appearance of a mentor or guide that can help you progress further in your work.

Finances
Since the High Priestess is related to mystery and the unknown, be wary of discussing your finances with others. This card suggests keeping your financial situation hidden. Alternatively, if you’re being presented with the opportunity to put your finances into use, your intuition will know whether this is a good choice or not. Take some time to probe your feelings; if there are red-flags, something won’t feel right. Listen to those feelings.

Feelings
Drawing The High Priestess invites you to delve into a deep, intuitive connection. This person is captivated by your mysterious aura and senses that there’s much more beneath the surface. Their feelings are instinctual rather than logical; they feel an undeniable pull towards you but remain cautious, wanting to understand the depths of your character before fully committing.

This card signals a time for self-reflection on your emotions. You may feel compelled to explore your inner self while wrestling with uncertainty about this relationship. Trusting your intuition will illuminate these complex feelings, guiding you as you uncover what truly resonates within and navigate this emotional landscape together.

Actions
The arrival of The High Priestess suggests that now is the time to turn inward and trust your intuition. You should focus on deepening your self-awareness and exploring your inner wisdom. This may involve setting aside quiet moments for meditation or journaling, allowing you to connect with your subconscious thoughts. Consider engaging in activities that foster creativity, such as painting or writing, which can help unlock hidden insights. Additionally, seek knowledge through reading spiritual texts or attending workshops that resonate with you. Embrace this period of reflection; it will guide you toward clarity and understanding in both personal and professional aspects of life.

Love
The Empress tarot love meaning stems from the element of earth. The person represented by this card can be loving, nurturing and caring, as has financial security or appreciative of beautiful, comforting things. Sometimes, the Empress can point to love and work coming together, either with a coworker, or perhaps a new business venture. When it comes to relationships, this card also heralds a stable, serious and committed relationship. Because the card also represents motherhood, sometimes it can also signal marriage or pregnancy, or at least a new family, in whatever form that means for you.

Career
Your career right now may be enjoying a boost right now. You may be more creative and passionate than usual, and putting all your ideas to work in your projects. Since the Empress is related to nourishment and nurturing, it may also suggest that you’re feeling particularly nurturing and generous when it comes to your workplace as well. You may be working on making a more harmonious and welcoming office, whether that means being supportive of coworkers, or putting a new coat of paint at your home office. Having the environment to do your best can certainly give you even more momentum. Sometimes, this card can also point to another person in your workplace that has these qualities.

Finances
The Empress is abundant both creatively and materially, so this card can point to a comfortable financial situation. You may also be feeling very generous with your money now, wanting to nourish your friends and family with your abundance and good luck. It is certainly a good time to share what you have.

Feelings
When you draw The Empress, someone is overflowing with warmth and affection for you. They see you as nurturing and abundant, drawn to your caring nature. You are a source of comfort and inspiration in their life, bringing beauty wherever you go. Their feelings are rooted in admiration and a desire for growth together, hinting at a future filled with love and harmony.
The arrival of The Empress signals a surge of creativity and emotional fulfillment in your life. You may feel more connected to your desires and instincts than ever before, fully embracing the joy that comes from self-love. This card urges you to nurture yourself while also recognizing the blossoming relationships around you.

Actions
Guided by The Empress, you are encouraged to embrace nurturing actions and creativity in your life. This card encourages you to cultivate a sense of abundance, both within yourself and in your surroundings. Focus on self-care by engaging in activities that bring you joy, such as gardening or cooking nourishing meals. Consider fostering relationships by reaching out to loved ones or creating a supportive community around you. Additionally, channel your creative energy into artistic projects or hobbies that inspire you. By embracing these nurturing actions, you'll not only enhance your well-being but also attract positivity and growth into your life.

Love

In romance, the upright Temperance tarot love meaning suggests patience, moderation, understanding and going the middle path. This card indicates that we must avoid going to extremes, and to be cautious and thoughtful of our actions. Consider your actions when it comes to love; and in what aspects your attitudes, beliefs or thoughts can be excessive. Are you too pushy with potential partners? Or instead, are you too reserved? Are you too giving? Or are you not giving enough? How can you bring these traits into balance? In addition, your relationship or potential relationships may require some patience right now, and attempt to work together to find compromise and harmony.

Career

Patience and moderation may be helpful tools for you to achieve your career goals. You are likely to find what you desire when it comes to your work, but it may come slowly and quietly as you put in the work every day. Your dedication and ability to navigate emotionally charged situations at work with calm can help you be noticed by your peers and superiors. When it comes to making changes in your career path, the Temperance card can be a reminder to remain patient, steady and devoted; all good things take time. Temperance can also signal doing a good job in balancing your career with different aspects of your life; it is neither an all consuming ambition or just a paycheck to you.

Finances

The Temperance card can be a call to make sure that your approach to your finances is one of moderation and balance. This can mean that you’ve been diligent with saving, while also being able to treat yourself with something you can afford every once in a while. Over time, you may be building your resources with steady, diligent saving.

Feelings

The upright Temperance card reveals a deep sense of balance and harmony in their feelings for you. They appreciate your presence, sensing a natural flow between you two that hints at potential growth and mutual understanding. Their emotions are rooted in patience and moderation, showing they value the connection without rushing into anything impulsive. In terms of your own feelings, Temperance urges you to find equilibrium within yourself. You may crave peace and stability as you navigate your emotions. This card encourages you to blend different aspects of your life harmoniously, prompting reflection on what truly brings you joy while keeping an open heart toward the possibilities this relationship holds.

Actions

With Temperance in your hands, it’s time to embrace balance and moderation in your life. You should focus on harmonizing different aspects of your existence, whether it’s work-life balance or emotional equilibrium. This may involve reassessing your daily routines to ensure they align with your values and goals. Consider incorporating mindfulness practices like meditation or yoga to cultivate inner peace. Additionally, engage in activities that promote collaboration rather than competition, fostering connections with others while maintaining healthy boundaries. Embrace patience as you blend various elements of your life into a cohesive whole, allowing for growth and transformation.

new beginning • spontaneity • leap of faith

A pelican is perched upon an ocean post, illuminated by a waning crescent moon. He piercingly regards a sodden lone wolf, cast among the waves, paddling through unfamiliar territory. Hoping for an easy dinner, he has foolishly swum out beyond the cautious trappings of his solid world. Gazing up at the stoic pelican, the wolf realizes he has departed on a journey that could easily result in his own demise.
 
The Fool represents a new beginning, striking out naively on a bold new adventure. You may be filled with unlimited optimism, a feeling in your heart that you cannot fail. This may prove misguided, and in due time you might find your idealism tempered by painful experience. So approach with caution: decide whether taking this risk is worth making yourself vulnerable in an unfamiliar setting. If the answer is yes, show no fear: only those who choose to journey will ever discover new horizons.

introspective • intuition • mystery of subconscious

The High Priestess is the ruler of the subconscious, where ideas are first conceived. Much like Persephone, she treads the surface of the under.world, brimming with insight but biding her time. When the moment is right, she will burst into the sunshine with all she has learned below. But for now, her footsteps ripple the water in the light of the waning moon, which calls for a quiet retreat of imagination and inner reflection.

Counterbalancing the raw power of the Magician, the High Priestess is the internal, introspective side of creation. She is the fertile subconscious where ideas are first brought to life. Also consider that action is not always the best possible step: sometimes it’s best to reflect, amass strength, and consider your options before beginning anew. This is not an indication of cowardice, but of wisdom.

notes.html: The overall meaning of the Four of Wands is that it heralds celebration as well as a harmonious, happy and relaxed home environment. In terms of numerology, the number four symbolizes stability as well as particularly reliable foundations. These are associated with a period of happiness and balance.

Love 
This card is the card of family, of reunions and of festivities. The 4 of Wands tarot love meaning can bring about engagements, marriages, or other gatherings that commemorate you and your love. If you’re in a stable relationship built on a strong foundation of trust, support and understanding, your union may be strengthened even more with the support and witness of your family and friends. This kind of love is not just the love between two people, but a love that is supported within the context of a larger community. Should you be single, you may find love within these communities and gatherings.

Career 
The upright four of wands is a stable and social card. It, when upright, signifies stable and supportive relationships. This sense of community applies to your work environment when it appears in this position. Possibly, you have made new friends at work or the atmosphere there has been particularly positive lately. There may also be work gatherings such as office parties in the near future aimed at bringing you closer to the people with whom you work. If there are, these events are likely to result in closer bonds between you and your colleagues.

Finances 
The four of wands here not only represents financial stability, but it also indicates that you can be spending that money on loved ones. You might be buying gifts or taking people you care about out for dinners or drinks. These are good financial decisions. They might not increase your financial wealth, but they are beneficial to your social relationships and thus you can embrace them. Do not go overboard on anything, but so long as you spend within your means, the cards are encouraging you to treat those around you.

Feelings
The upright Four of Wands reveals a heart brimming with joy and celebration. This person feels a strong sense of harmony and stability in your connection, recognizing that it brings them happiness and belonging. They envision shared moments filled with laughter and warmth, cherishing the solid foundation you've built together.

Your own feelings mirror this sentiment, reflecting deep contentment and excitement about the future. You’re inspired by the possibilities ahead, welcoming the idea of commitment or partnership. Gratitude fills your energy for what you’ve created so far, urging you to celebrate both your personal growth and the bond you’ve nurtured together.

Actions
With the Four of Wands in your hands, it’s time to celebrate and embrace community. You should focus on nurturing your relationships and creating joyful experiences with loved ones. Consider organizing a gathering or event to strengthen bonds, whether it’s a simple dinner party or a larger celebration. This card encourages you to appreciate the stability in your life, so take moments to express gratitude for what you have built together with others. Embrace this energy by engaging in activities that foster connection, such as volunteering or collaborating on projects that bring people together, reinforcing your sense of belonging and joy.

When the Ace of Chalices presents itself, some deep wellspring of emotional force is bubbling up inside you or around you. It promises the beginnings of an intimate connection, guided by the heart. Open yourself to love and compassion. Draw deep feelings to the surface and let them shine.
