Consider creating traditions that strengthen bonds and foster a sense of belonging. Additionally, think about your financial future; take steps towards long-term stability by budgeting wisely or exploring investment opportunities. Embrace a mindset of abundance and gratitude, recognizing the wealth already present in your life while actively working towards securing it for generations to come.

Source: https://labyrinthos.co/blogs/tarot-card-meanings-list/ten-of-pentacles-meaning-tarot-card-meanings

LOVE

The person symbolized by the Page of Pentacles is ambitious, loyal and practical; they may often be seen as studious, but once you get to know them well, they can also be quite funny. Their ambition and focus means that they are hardworking. They are likely to be as dedicated as they are to a lover, as they are to their goals. Their quiet demeanor may make them hard to notice at first, compared to other folks that may be more out going.
If this doesn’t represent a person that is entering your love life, the Page of Pentacles tarot love meaning can simply signal this Page’s dedication and loyalty in your relationship. While sometimes the relationship can lack passion and feel a bit boring, the love is there; you may only need to go out there and figure out how to inject some fun and excitement back into your romance. Try not to always put practicality before passion in the relationship and the two of you should be just fine.

CAREER

You may now be building a strong foundation for success. You’re likely to be creating your goals, planning strategies and putting those plans into action. You’re not afraid to put yourself out there in order to achieve your wildest dreams. It is likely that there are lots of work opportunities available for you, so go ahead and reach for them! Sometimes, this card can also suggest that you are going through or looking to start a higher education program. Study hard; if you do the work, you’re likely to do an amazing job.

FINANCES

Good news is coming in regards to your finances. The Page of Pentacles promises good rewards, so long as you take the steps to plan your future. Do the research, stay on track with your budget, and you’ll be seeing that your effort will make a big difference in your material situation.

FEELINGS

The Page of Pentacles reveals a sense of curiosity and admiration. If you're wondering how someone feels about you, they see potential in your connection and are excited to explore what could blossom between you. They appreciate your grounded nature and feel inspired by your ambition and dedication. Their feelings are practical, emphasizing their desire for stability and growth in relationships. As for your own feelings, the Page of Pentacles signals a renewed sense of hope and enthusiasm. You’re reflecting on your goals while considering how this relationship fits into them. There’s an eagerness within you to nurture this bond, along with a strong desire for personal development alongside someone who shares your values.

ACTIONS

When you draw the upright Page of Pentacles, you’re being asked to embrace a mindset of curiosity and practicality. You should focus on setting tangible goals, whether it’s starting a new project or enhancing your skills through education. This card encourages you to explore opportunities for growth, so consider enrolling in a course or seeking mentorship in an area that excites you. Additionally, take small but deliberate steps towards financial stability by budgeting wisely or investing in something meaningful. By adopting this proactive approach and nurturing your ambitions with patience, you'll cultivate both personal satisfaction and future success.

Source: https://labyrinthos.co/blogs/tarot-card-meanings-list/page-of-pentacles-meaning-tarot-card-meanings

LOVE

The Knight of Pentacles is hardworking and diligent. He is patient, reliable and steady, though sometimes deeply absorbed in his work. They prefer not to take risks in love, as well as elsewhere in their lives. It is difficult to get this person to change their minds; which means they can be stubborn, but also a very trustworthy and dedicated partner. The Knight of Pentacles tarot love meaning can also suggest a relationship that is deep and reliable, but not very exciting. If you’re at a point where you would like commitment, stability and security in your love life, this card can be a welcome sight. It indicates a partnership in which both of you will be working towards your long term goals together.

CAREER

When it comes to work, the Knight of Pentacles suggests ambition, drive and focus. You are very much committed to your goals, however far away in the future they may be. It’s likely that you’ll do anything you can do achieve them, so you’re prepared to put in the hard work and the blood, sweat and tears. You have a slow and steady approach, and believe that hard work is rewarded. Should you be searching for a job, you’ll need to prove your reliability and your dedication to a prospective employer.

FINANCES

The Knight of Pentacles builds his financial future slowly, but steadily. He avoids taking big risks, and prefers things that are as safe and reliable as he is. You may be budgeting and slowly saving for a long term goal. Some frugality may be helpful now.

FEELINGS

The Knight of Pentacles reveals a steadfast and reliable energy in how this person feels about you. They see you as someone deserving of their time and effort, prioritizing stability and commitment over fleeting emotions. Their feelings are rooted in practicality; they value your consistency and dedication, which builds trust between you. This individual approaches their feelings with patience, aiming to create something lasting rather than rushing into impulsive decisions. Reflecting on your own emotions, the Knight of Pentacles indicates a desire for security and reliability in this connection. You may find comfort in taking things slow, nurturing what’s already present instead of chasing immediate gratification. Embrace the journey ahead with diligence, recognizing that true fulfillment often stems from steady progress rather than hasty choices.

ACTIONS

In terms of diligence, this card invites reflection on your responsibility in your pursuits. Focus on setting clear, achievable goals and take consistent steps toward them. This card encourages you to adopt a methodical approach; create a detailed plan for your projects or tasks, ensuring each step is practical and grounded. Consider organizing your workspace or finances to foster productivity. Additionally, cultivate patience as progress may be slow but steady. Embrace this moment as an opportunity to build a solid foundation for future success through hard work and commitment to your values.

Source: https://labyrinthos.co/blogs/tarot-card-meanings-list/knight-of-pentacles-meaning-tarot-card-meanings

LOVE

The Queen of Pentacles is a worldly, practical, generous, hardworking and warm person, who has a talent both for business as well as a love of comfort and luxury. She enjoys making her home welcoming, always delighted to have guests. Single folks right now should be in a wonderful position to choose a partner that truly brings something into your life. You’ll likely have high standards, and hope for someone who has the same level of dedication, commitment and ambition as you do. If you’re already in a relationship, you may find that the two of you are enjoying a stable, fruitful and prosperous time in your life together. You can certainly afford to indulge a little and treat yourselves.

CAREER

When it comes to all things career oriented, the Queen of Pentacles tarot card can bring great success. She is a talented businesswoman who is practical, organized and very capable in anything she puts her mind to. In your life, she can appear as a successful person, who may make a great mentor, colleague or business partner. If you do choose to collaborate with her, you’ll find that her vast skill set will be invaluable to your career or your professional projects. If she offers advice, listen to it; she cares for you, and will help you accomplish your goals.

FINANCES

The Queen of Pentacles offers abundance, success, and material security. You may find that after a period of hard work, you have all that you need to feel comfortable. This card represents a responsible person, who knows how to balance enjoying life’s pleasures, with practicality, frugality and good taste. She’ll always look for a good deal, but will never compromise on quality.

FEELINGS

The Queen of Pentacles reveals that this person sees you as a comforting presence, someone who embodies security and warmth. They feel grounded with you, appreciating how you create an emotionally safe space. Their admiration for your ability to balance ambition with care draws them to you on both emotional and practical levels. Your feelings reflect a sense of abundance and fulfillment. You’re likely contemplating what truly matters: your values, relationships, and personal growth. A strong desire stirs within you to pursue your goals while also prioritizing self-care and nurturing your own needs alongside those of others.

ACTIONS

When you draw the upright Queen of Pentacles, you’re being asked to nurture both yourself and your surroundings. Embrace a mindset of abundance and practicality, focusing on creating a stable environment. This could mean organizing your home or investing in self-care routines that promote well-being. Consider reaching out to loved ones, offering support or guidance, as this will strengthen your connections. Additionally, explore ways to enhance your financial security through budgeting or planning for future investments. By embodying this nurturing energy, you cultivate not only personal growth but also foster a sense of community around you.

Source: https://labyrinthos.co/blogs/tarot-card-meanings-list/queen-of-pentacles-meaning-tarot-card-meanings

LOVE

Successful, generous, dependable and protective, the person represented by the King of Pentacles makes for a great partner, parent, and provider. He is demonstrative of his love through action instead of words, and looks to create a stable and loving home for his family. If you meet this person, they may be slow to make a commitment, but this is only because they take love very seriously, and need to truly understand you before taking any next steps. While not representing a person, the King of Pentacles can suggest a time in your relationship which is secure and stable. The two of you will be very comfortable, both emotionally with each other, and materially. You may have worked very hard in the past to enjoy your current standards of living, and you can now relax.

CAREER

In a professional context, the King of Pentacles can be an outstanding indicator of a successful business venture. When it comes to your work and your career, this King achieves his highest ambitions and has a great reputation amongst his colleagues. This card can additionally indicate that someone with more experience will mentor and encourage you in your chosen field. This person will have lots of experience, and can give you much needed support, and sometimes even recommendations to new jobs, or promotions.

FINANCES

When it comes to finances, the King of Pentacles represents an achievement of a financial milestone. Perhaps you have reached a level of security that comes from being diligent and wisely saving and investing. Since this King is also generous, you may also be using your newfound wealth to support loved ones, while enjoying the luxuries that you may have missed out on while you were saving. Indulge a little, you deserve it.

FEELINGS

The upright King of Pentacles reveals a profound sense of stability and security in how this person feels about you. They see you as someone deserving of their time and investment, valuing your grounded nature and reliability. Their feelings are practical, envisioning a lasting connection built on trust and mutual respect. This individual is protective and nurturing, eager to create a solid foundation together. The King of Pentacles also reflects your own desire for stability and commitment. You’re drawn to dependable energy, recognizing the value others bring into your life. In your feelings for another, you appreciate the tangible bond between you two, fostering comfort that invites deeper emotional exploration.

ACTIONS

When you draw the King of Pentacles, you’re being asked to embrace your leadership qualities and take charge of your financial and material well-being. Focus on building stability in your life by setting clear goals for your career or investments. Consider creating a budget or investing in personal development, such as taking a course that enhances your skills. This card encourages you to adopt a mindset of abundance; visualize success and act with confidence. Surround yourself with supportive individuals who share similar ambitions, as collaboration can lead to fruitful opportunities. Your actions today will lay the groundwork for future prosperity.

Associated with the element of Water and the aspect of the heart, the suit of cups in the Tarot holds several beautiful connective cards. 

With this suit, we explore emotions, relationships, love and friendship, community, intuition, faith, spirituality, creativity, and magic, diving into our own sense of inner wisdom with sensitivity, wonder, and delight.

And while we tend to think of this as the suit of love, cups also acknowledge the harder emotions we can experience: sorrow, loneliness, anger, frustration, sadness, and grief. Just like Water itself, the suit of cups holds endless depths, raging currents, and rich beauty.

Cups represent the heart. It helps us acknowledge our most tender and personal feelings, the people and communities we feel drawn to, the ways that we need to be held and understood.

In addition to Water and the heart, the suit of cups also represents creativity, attachment, attraction, love, family, connection, art, beauty, intimacy, vulnerability, empathy, perception, and intuition.

Just like the astrological element of Water, it’s here that we explore the depths that we carry, the secrets we keep, the times that we are fluid, and the times that we are stagnant.

As we move through the suit of cups, we discover a new wellspring of emotion, build important connections, grapple with loneliness and disappointment, reflect on our histories, make important decisions about where to invest emotional energy, and find ourselves fully supported by the collective.
When working with cards in the suit of cups, remember that these cards ask us to explore a particularly complex topic and may help us dig into feelings or reactions that we haven’t always completely acknowledged.

Where are you afraid to explore?
What secrets do you keep from yourself, and how do boundaries of protection help you heal and grow?
How does connection with others help us more fully understand ourselves?

The pips in the suit of cups show us many ways that we can think about this energy, from opening our hearts to new connections to guarding it when we feel unsafe. These cards can help us recognize and hold space for our own grief or hurt, push us to be more generous with our energy, and extend empathy or kindness in new ways.

The court cards, on the other hand, represent individuals that are learning how to utilize the energy of the cups best. The page is a child and student, someone who is just beginning their journey with creativity and sensitivity; the knight is an adolescent, eager to prove their talent and desire with actions; the queen is a master and ruler who teaches others how to use this element internally, and the king is a master and ruler who teaches others how to use this element externally. These cards can represent the querent, a person in the querent’s life, or can offer advice on how to harness the energy of the suit of cups for themselves.

Working With Cups
For a lot of people, seeing cards from the suit of cups is a joyful thing. After all, love is one of the most popular topics for tarot readings, and many people want to know more about the connections they may find and develop throughout their lives.

But it’s important to remember that these cards also have a lot to teach us about how we experience the world, the impact that art and beauty, and connection and sensitivity can have on us. Spend time with these cards individually, and consider the lessons they may hold for you as an individual, rather than just focusing on what they may have to say within the context of relationships.

This card represents the spark of new opportunity in the realms of all that is earthly: matter, body, and even wealth. The world brought forth by this card is fertile, and full of abundance bringing opportunity for prosperity.

A game of balance is what is at work here. This card gives the sense that rapid change has become a norm in your situation. Having to deal with opposing forces is unavoidable in certain circumstances, but luckily, you've had the resilience to be able to deal with them.
Several people of vastly varying skills and beliefs work together to join in on a greater cause. Teamwork helps to create something new. Progress is swift.

Vast wealth has been accumulated here, and as a result, you have become protective of what you have earned. Though some amount of conservatism is good for one's feeling of stability, this card can also warn of stinginess, and having a miserly attitude.
A time of need and desperation. Sometimes signals difficulties with one's relationship to money. But this card also signals that there is help available if one chooses only to see and acknowledge it.

Compassion and understanding breeds generosity, sharing and charity. One gives away the fruits of one's labours with the understanding that the situation of having the upper hand can be reversed at any moment.

An immense amount of work has been done, and the effort that has been put in previously is now ready to be harvested. Though the crop is ready, there is still more work, and it is now a time of focus and diligence before one can reap the rewards.

This card stresses the importance of hard work and diligence in accomplishing your goals. It indicates a time to buckle down, study, achieve new skills all in the name of being able to change your circumstances.

After much hard work, this card indicates a time of opulence and luxury, all resulting in a feeling of satisfaction, emotional comfort and peace. All of this is due to one's intelligence and self-control and represents an achievement that has lasted over a lifetime.
Represents the culmination of life's journeys. There's a sense of fulfillment that usually results from hard work in all of life's facets. This is the end of the path, and it is full of joy.

A man of utmost diligence - he knows he wants and is relentless in his pursuit of it. He is a hard worker, completinh his mission with complete and terrible efficiency. Although his path is long and hard, filled with tasks that might be repetitive and tiring, giving up is not an option.

A woman that is blessed with the gifts of sensual comforts and domestic talents. A motherly figure at times, she seeks to bring to her loved ones joy through all things that are worldly - by cooking, cleaning and creating a wonderful home.

The fruits of worldly ambition have brought financial success, a sense of abundance, stabilty and security. The king of pentacles is a fatherly figure that provides all of those things, and is also someone that is happy to share all that he has accumulated.
As with other ace cards, the ace of cups symbolozies new beginnings. It is the start of a feelign of emotional fulfillement - and reprensets the job of giving, and getting in return,
Signalling a union and partnership of balance, honour and respect. The ancient symbol of the caduceus also suggests energy, passion and sex, and the intermingling of opposite forces.

A warm and lively gathering of friends. You are blessed with loiving relationships and camadarie, and this is likely a very social period in your life where you are investing time in the people around you.

Being so deep in contemplation and thought, you may sometimes ignore the gifts that the world gives you. The potential joys that are laid at your feet are ignored. Even though your intentions may be noble, you run the risk of treating the world with apathy.

This card signifies the despair and sadness associated with loss. Three of the cups are overturned, but two of them are still upright, indicating that there is still a chance to salvage what has been lost.

The happy meeting between past and present is indicated here. There is a sense of wonderful nostalgia for times long ago. The memories coming back though, can sometimes be so engrossing that you begin to forget your present.

A range of choices present themselves to you, some of which promise power, riches, victory and love, and others that instead present you with disaster. Danger lurks within the choices, and wishful thinking and fantasy can lead one into trouble.

There is a feeling of disappointment and loss associated with this card. One has taken a retrospective of their situation and has decided to leave it behind. Something is abandoned, and through that abandonment, one feels the loss of a part of themselves.

An environment of luxury and emotional stability, where all available comforts await you. Indulging in all the joys that life has to offer you is signaled by this card, though at times there is a sense of smugness that comes from taking your situation for granted.

Emotional fulfilment and happiness due to a deep sense of unity with the world around you. This card is about harmony and the joy that results from it, applying to your family, friends and loved ones. There is a deep sense of community associated with this card.

The page of cups heralds a happy surprise of some kind. The fish that pops out of the cup is a signal that one's uncoscious is attempting to make contact, though sometimes one does not understand what is meant to be said.
A man who is in touch with his emotions and intuition and is able to channel them into action. It can signal an arrival or an invitation into something that will be the cause of celebration.
A figure in your life that is nurturing, compassionate, and able to instinctively understand the emotions of others. Because of this, they are usually generous and kind hearted.

A man whose greatest quality is his ability to control, balance and master his emotions. He is not empty of feelings, but rather full of them - only, he understands when and where they are appropriate and beneficial, and when they are harmful. He is a man of compassion, diplomacy and generosity.

The potential for immense power and success. But remember that the sword is double-edged - depending on who wields it, its power can be used to shelter and protect or to mercilessly strike down for cold and ruthless self-gain.

Being at crossroads, this is a moment when you must make a difficult choice. One path closes the other and your decision is hanging in a perfect equilibrium and balance, making the choice ever more difficult. There is no clear winner, but to progress, one must take a stand.

Suffering and heartbreak stemming from loneliness, rejection and betrayal. This card indicates a period of intense suffering. Moments like this are sometimes required in life in order to bring out the strength we never we had within us.

Rest after a period of intense struggle and heartbreak. Much has been lost recently, but this card indicates that one is in recovery from that challenge. The message being conveyed here is that in order to move forward and rejoin life, we must pause and look within.

Victory has been achieved, though it came with a subtle consequence. By taking from your opponents their ability to fight back in some form or fashion, you might have also created resentment. Your actions have isolated you from those who could be helpful later on.

A journey far from home has been initiated by past sorrows. But this journey is something that must be undertaken in order to move ahead. You are leaving a painful place and going into a distant environment that promises more potential

Deception is at work here. You might feel pressured to be dishonest in order to achieve your ambitions, hoping that these lies have gone unnoticed. This card is a warning of how difficult that can be.

This woman in the card is restrained and trapped, and indicates that she feels like there is no way out. But these feelings of helplessness are actually one that is cause by a belief in one's own victimization.

This represents someone that is trapped by their own negative thoughts. There is not necessarily a situation that warrants the worry, and this card hints that over-analysis leads to criplling indecision and feelings of helplessness.
Disaster strikes when one least expects it - it is swift and in this case, unavoidable. Something here is beyond your control, leaving you with a feeling that you are a victim of your circumstances.

The page of swords represents someone embarking on a new idea and a mental adventure. Full of enthusiasm and good cheer, this person is eager to share and discuss their thoughts and plans for what can be.

The power of an idea to overwhelm is represented by the Knight of Swords. Filled with the vision of an idea, he is propelled forward with unbridled ambition. Though his energy is great, there is also a warning associated with being uncouscious about consequences and obstacles.
A woman of immense complexity, sometimes considered cold-hearted, but also sharp of mind and wit, independent and possessing great powers of organization and analysis

With sharp intellect and clarity of mind, the king of swords is a representative of truth and its authority. He cuts through deception and is able to rule with a stern and calm intellect. He serves as an incorruptible pillar of strength through his calm of mind.

The suit of wands is always the first step in the act of creation. It is the burning fire of intention, desire and passion that ignites the spark of an idea. Thus, this card represents the powerful forces of your will guiding your way like a torch into the world, on a journey to make these desires come into reality.
The transformation of vision and ambition into planning and progress. Starting to move into a way forward. The man beholds the material in which he can make his designs come true.

Represents the transformation of dreams into concrete plans and preparation for action. As you look forward to the possible obstacles in your path, you remain dedicated to your pursuit and ready to traverse your boundaries.

A celebration of harmony, happiness and good relationships. It is a time of peace after a period of hard work. The four of wands usually indicates this in regards to family and large groups of people.

A battle between rivals. There is a struggle from all sides for dominance. Although they may seem intimidating at first, there is also the impression that they pose no dire threat - possibly being more of a show of power than actual intention to do true harm.
After a tough battle, the six of wands represents a very public celebration of a victory. It is achievement as well as recognition for one's achievements.
Even with success, the battle is never over. After achieving a victory and a higher position, one must also put up a defense against the many competitors that want to wrench away your laurels.

After the struggle, there is a time of quick movement and unstoppable action. You have an overflowing of energy and spirit to add to your tasks and your projects. Absolute and piercing willpower combined with swift and sure execution.

You are close to achieving a victory after a time of battle and hard work. You have spent time pursuing what you believe to be right, though this was difficult and draining. You are reaching a point of exhaustion, but there is only a small way to go before your ultimate goal.

The ten of wands indicates that you have been working extremely hard in order to turn something into fruition. At the end of that journey however, you find yourself being overburdened and too heavy with the responsibility that you created for yourself.

You are on the brink of a new creative project and vision, there is a spirit of discovery and enthusiasm in all kinds of ideas that you might have about the future. It is the start of new way of expressing oneself.

This person is a man of action - he represents the manifestation of an idea and the passionate pursuit of a vision. Because this person is highly focused on action, he can also be brash, impulsive and unrealistic,
Represents a feminine aspect which is fiery, determined, and strong. Like the other wand suits, she is a natural leader whose courage in the face of adversity is an inspiration to all around her.
A person having great vision and leadership, and all the drive and understanding to create his vision. He leads and inspires others with his unconquerable passion.

Skullcap: Herb of Meditation. Calms the mind and heart and prepares the way to meditation. Its tonic properties will help the inner channel of inspiration to be strengthened so that inner truths can be brought forth and manifested in life. Many times when we have realizations, our bodies and especially our nerves and heart must be prepared to handle the accelerated energy flow. Skullcap seems to have the capacity to strengthen the nerves of the body to receive the inspirations so that they do not create chaos and turbulence in us due to the changes they engender.

Lemon Balm: Herb of Evolution. Balances the feelings and the emotions & helps resolve moodiness and melancholia. It was sacred to alchemists, and the plant-based philosopher’s stone is made from an alchemical preparation of this plant. In a metaphorical sense, Melissa guides us as we traverse the misty emotional state of the Moon and enables us to view our emotions and feelings without getting lost in them.

Angelica: Herb of Warmth and Compassion. Said to be the herb of angels and to enable one to commune with the angelic realm. It has been used to bring good energy and fortune into one’s life. One can partake in the energy of angelica in many ways. As a ritual bath it can strengthen the aura and bring joy to one’s essence. When burned as an incense or smudge it gives off a pungent aroma that will help protect and purify the area. It helps open up the heart energy and allows one to traverse the heart’s path with more peace and clarity. Wearing angelica as an amulet will remind the wearer of the lessons of the Sun card and will help the wearer to follow the heart’s path with faith and certainty.

Goldenseal: Herb of Awakening. Has the capacity to clear out the old congested ways and make way for the new. Bitter emotions such as grief and astringent emotions such as fear are cleared away and replaced with a purified palate for life. This powerful herb has the ability to bring clarity as to what our purpose is in being here and can help us confront the fears and misgivings we may have about expressing and living our inner truths. Its pungent smell can help change our inner attitude about ourselves.

The Suit of Cups deals with the emotional level of consciousness and is associated with love, feelings, relationships and connections.

It is associated with the element of water. Water is fluid, agile and ‘in flow’ but it’s also very powerful and formative. It can be soft and gentle, like waves lapping against the sandy shore, or it can be powerful and even forceful, like a raging river.

The element of water is symbolic of fluidity, feelings and emotions, intuition, relationships, healing, and cleansing. It is a feminine element and reflects the subtle power that often resides within women. It is receptive, adaptable, purifying and flowing.

In a deck of playing cards, Cups corresponds to Hearts.

What do Cups mean in a reading?
Cups Tarot cards indicate that you are thinking with your heart rather than your head, and thus reflect your spontaneous responses and your habitual reactions to situations. Cups are also linked to creativity, romanticism, fantasy and imagination.

The negative aspects of the Suit of Cups include being overly emotional or completely disengaged and dispassionate, having unrealistic expectations and fantasising about what could be. There may be repressed emotions, an inability to truly express oneself and a lack of creativity.

Cups Tarot cards often represent the astrological signs of Water – Pisces, Cancer, and Scorpio. When you see a Cups Court Card in a Tarot reading, it often relates to a person with a Pisces, Cancer, and Scorpio star sign. Generally, Cups people are emotional, artistic, humane and creative. They are connected with their emotional selves and will draw energy from what they feel within.

What Does it Mean When a  Reading is Mostly Cups?
Should a Tarot reading be predominantly Cups cards, you are seeking solutions to what are primarily emotional conflicts, personal interactions, love matters, feelings and creativity.

notes.html:
The Suit of Swords deals with the mental level of consciousness that is centered around the mind and the intellect. Swords mirror the quality of mind present in your thoughts, attitudes, and beliefs.

Swords are often double-edged and in this way the Suit of Swords symbolises the fine balance between intellect and power and how these two elements can be used for good or evil. As such, the Swords must be balanced by spirit (Wands) and feeling (Cups) to have the most positive effect.

It is associated with the element of Air. Air is intangible and unseen, but also in constant movement. Air can be still and mostly unnoticed, to becoming a breeze or a fierce wind. It is powerful yet refreshing and cleansing. Symbolically, the air element relates to knowledge, action, power, and change. It is a masculine energy that can lead by force and power, even though it remains unseen.

In a deck of playing cards, Swords corresponds to Spades.

What Do the Swords Tarot Cards Mean in a Reading?
The Suit of Swords Tarot card meanings are associated with action, change, force, power, oppression, ambition, courage and conflict. Action can be constructive and/or destructive.

The negative aspects of the Suit of Swords include anger, guilt, harsh judgement, a lack of compassion and verbal and mental abuse.

Swords Tarot cards often represent the astrological signs of Air – Aquarius, Libra and Gemini. When you see a Swords Court Card in a Tarot reading, it often relates to a person with a Aquarius, Libra and Gemini star sign. Generally, Swords people are intelligent, thoughtful, rational, logical and excellent communicators. They are rational beings and like to experience the world by understanding and analysing what is occurring around them. On the flipside, Swords people can be ruthless, domineering, confrontational and rigid.

What Does it Mean When a Reading is Mostly Swords?
Should a Tarot reading be predominantly Swords cards, you are seeking solutions to what are primarily mental struggles, conflict and arguments, and decisions that must be made. Also, there could be many arguments or even violence at present. While Swords can carry with them many negative or very strong, forceful messages, Swords serve also as a warning to be more cautious of what is occurring around you.

The Suit of Wands meanings are associated with primal energy, spirituality, inspiration, determination, strength, intuition, creativity, ambition and expansion, original thought and the seeds through which life springs forth.

It is associated with the element of Fire. Fire is hot, wild, unpredictable, and energetic. It can be creative in helping us to cook food or build tools, or it can be destructive, like a devastating bush fire or house fire.

Fire is symbolic of passion, energy, enthusiasm, and sexuality. It is a masculine element and reflects the drive and willpower of the masculine energy.

In a deck of playing cards, Wands corresponds to Clubs.


What Do Wands Mean In A Reading?
The meanings of the Wands Tarot cards deal with the spiritual level of consciousness and mirror what is important to you at the core of your being. They address what makes you tick – your personality, ego, enthusiasm, self-concept, and personal energy, both internal and external.

The negative aspects of the Suit of Wands include illusion, egotistical behaviour, impulsiveness, a lack of direction or purpose, or feeling meaningless.

Wands often represent the astrological signs of Fire – Leo, Sagittarius and Aries. When you see a Wands Court Card in a Tarot reading, it often relates to a person with a Leo, Sagittarius or Aries star sign. Generally, Wands people are energetic, charismatic, warm, spiritual.

When A Tarot Reading Is Mostly Wands, you can be sure that you are seeking solutions to issues that are based mainly in the realm of thought, or that are in the first stages of development. You may also be seeking greater purpose and meaning in your life and will want to understand more about what motivates and energises you.

The Suit of Pentacles deal with the physical or external level of consciousness and thus mirror the outer situations of your health, finances, work, and creativity. They have to do with what we make of our outer surroundings – how we create it, shape it, transform it and grow it. On a more esoteric level, Pentacles are associated with the ego, self-esteem and self-image.

It is associated with the element of Earth. Earth is tactile, earthy and tangible. It creates the foundation from which the planet can grow and develop, and it supports and nurtures the plants and trees. Earth is grounded, stable, supportive and fertile. It is a feminine element that is receptive – it takes in nutrients and sunrays and then uses this energy to sustain the life that grows out of it.

In a deck of playing cards, Pentacles corresponds to Diamonds.

What Do Pentacles  Mean In A Reading?
The Suit of Pentacles meanings cover material aspects of life including work, business, trade, property, money and other material possessions. The positive aspects of the Suit of Pentacles include manifestation, realisation, proof and prosperity.

The negative aspects of the Suit of Pentacles include being possessive, greedy and overly materialistic, over-indulging and not exercising, not effectively managing one's finances, and being overly focused on career to the detriment of other life priorities. Often what is required to counteract these negative aspects is a return to nature to ground oneself and rediscover what is truly important.

Pentacles Tarot cards often represent the astrological signs of Earth – Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. When you see a Pentacles Court Card in a Tarot reading, it often relates to a person with a Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn star sign. Generally, Pentacles people are practical, career-minded, down-to-earth and generous. They are tactile beings and like to experience the physical, tangible world. They are connected through the senses and seek pleasurable and sometimes indulgent experiences.

Should a Tarot reading be predominantly Pentacles cards, you are seeking solutions to what are primarily material conflicts, financial matters and concerns with career and work.

Comfrey: Herb of Unity. Helps us to knit our realities and our lives together. Meditations with the herb or the card will enable us to understand better how the world with all its segments is pulled together by the unity of the Divine Creative Energy behind all manifestation. We will see more clearly how to be focused and present so that our visions can be joyfully manifested.

Yarrow:  has the capacity to open the mind and the seventh chakra to inspirations and revelations from Spirit. It is cleansing to the body and the aura and will offer protection against invasive thought forms. One will hear one’s own internal music more clearly as the blockages are cleared.
Basil: Basil will help develop, reveal, and use the enthusiastic fire element within. It supports idealism and keeps inner vision clear.

Saffron: helps to stimulate the digestion of experiences and will help in the healthful assimilation of the lessons learned. It will impart the energy of love and devotion and will help one to see one’s part in the dance of life more clearly.

Fennel: allows a greater sense of groundedness and joy to permeate one’s being. Rub fennel oil on the soles of the feet and dance to the rhythms of life. Crush a fresh sprig of fennel and let its smell fill you with healing earth energy and help you to release any hesitations you may have with regards to finishing the project at hand. Play with life more and find friends with whom you can share some fun.

Turmeric: When one feels a lack of strength and spiritual power, this herb will fortify and create an inner stirring of strength. For those whose energy is aggressive and argumentative, it will clear this energy and create the space for a new and healthier viewpoint to grow.

Wild Ginger: Presenting a perfect heart-shaped leaf, wild ginger is naturally found in the shaded areas of forests. Here it serves to remind us not to lose heart even as we pass through the densest thicket and the darkest moments of our life. It will stimulate in us the need to be brave and to face our fears with spiritual tenacity.

Sassafras: opens up the fifth chakra (throat) and allows easier communication of ideas. It enhances the connection you have with angelic beings that watch over you. Sassafras affords you greater psychic protection against the negative effects of external harassment and attack. It will ward off or lessen the blows of conflicting forces.

Bayberry Bark: strengthens and coalesces reserves in the face of adversity and opposition. Areas of inner conflict and self-invalidation will be made more visible, and the energy of attracting conflict toward the self will be lessened.

Prickly Ash Bark: relieves feelings of oppression and burden. The idea that one is a martyr and victim will slowly be transformed to seeing the self as a creator and a responsible being. There is no need for or virtue in chewing and digesting someone else’s experiences and lessons. It will be seen that it is better to allow others to face their own karma and responsibility while you remain in detached compassion.

The sense is of being overwhelmed, oppressed, and weighted down by various cares and concerns. While there is less opportunity for distractions and diversions, there is an obvious opportunity for organizing and gaining clearer focus and vision. Adhering to priorities can generate focused energy that will bring the reward of important personal breakthroughs.

Take the opportunity to become organized in all aspects of your being. Clarify your goals. Make sure you allow others to take on their responsibilities as well. There is no need for you to take on other people’s loads. A lot can be accomplished when this energy is handled properly.
Shepherd’s-purse: invigorates the life-force within and helps one to recognize and implement talents and abilities that have been hidden. It strengthens the will and spiritual tenacity.
Aconite: may be carried as a talisman to maximize potential and overcome indifference and apathy. It will stimulate the fire within and help one to move out of fixed conditions.
Raspberry Leaf: helps one tune into the child within and allows natural enthusiasm for life to be manifested. It will soften the heart and allow for greater receptivity and intuition.
Cinnamon: helps build the internal fire and will. Its warm energy can dissipate inner coldness and allow the creative fires to burn.

Associated with Fire and the aspect of the soul, the suit of wands brings with it a sensation of intensity, inspiration, and creativity.

The fastest-moving suit in the deck and one associated with passion, creation, and ambition, this suit urges us to make space for our biggest, brightest, most powerful dreams to tap into the things that inspire and motivate us. And as exciting as it can be to throw our full selves into the things that we hope to achieve, the suit of wands also carries warnings around friction, destruction, and burnout.

Wands Basics
Wands  connected to the astrological element of Fire, meaning that this suit is also linked to the three Fire zodiac signs: Aries,Leo, and Sagittarius.

Wands represent the soul. Wands help us understand the things that drive us, the urges and instincts that motivate us, the pursuits and desires that give our life shape and meaning.

As well as Fire and the soul, the suit of wands also explores passion, attraction,
motivation, sensuality, artistic endeavors, instincts, creativity, exploration, expansion, and adventure.

Just like the astrological element of Fire, it’s here that we dig deep into the desires of our deepest and truest self. We seek the richest sense of authenticity, work to understand what inspires us, build something that feels reflective of our greatest passions. As we move through the suit of wands, we follow a burst of energy and creativity from that initial flash of inspiration to building, collaboration, friction and frustration, new beginnings, independence, and eventually to an abundance of Fire or a sensation of burnout.

Fire can be difficult to control, and in learning to balance it with other elements, sometimes we find that it takes over, overwhelming us with its intensity.

When working with the suit of wands, keep in mind that these cards may be speaking to a creative project, an artistic dream, or a passionate interest that has been demanding more of your time.

How do you decide what to focus on? When do you trust your instincts?
How do you recognize when an idea is worth your time and energy, and
when do you allow yourself to step back and look more closely at your work?

The pips (or numbered cards) in the suit of wands show us many ways to think about this energy, from finding joy and a sense of empowerment through what we are building to guarding our energy and not letting our natural Fire overtake us. There are moments when we are called to action, asked to take courage.

But there are also moments when we are asked to step back from movement and assess our choices, consider ways to slow down, and be cautious about how we are spending our energy.

On the other hand, the court cards represent individuals learning how to utilize the energy of the wands best.
The page is a child and student, someone who is just beginning their journey with passion and excitement; the knight is an adolescent, eager to prove their talent and skill with confident actions; the queen is a master and ruler who teaches others how to use this element internally, and the king is a master and ruler who teaches others how to use this element externally.
These cards can represent the querent, a person in the querent’s life, or can offer advice on how to harness the energy of the suit of wands for themselves.

Working With Wands
Within the suit of wands, we find some of the highest highs and lowest lows in the minor arcana, as the ways that we harness and utilize creative energy can be intensely personal.

The fire that dwells within us sometimes acts as tiny sparks and other times as an intoxicating blaze, and no matter where in that process we are, the Tarot can help us understand our own brilliance more clearly.

notes.html: Chamomile: bestows greater inner peace and finer clarity about one’s inner spiritual purpose.  Chamomile has the ability to enhance visions and to bring them into form on the earth.

Passion flower:  said to pacify the spirit. As an herbal essence it will impart a sense of peaceful balance and tranquility. Meditations with the flower can be quite mesmerizing, similar to looking at a mandala. It brings focus and accord to the mind and heart.

Pleurisy Root: Many times grief and sadness becomes stuck in the lungs and manifests as congestion and phlegm. An herbal essence of pleurisy root may help to relieve old emotions that need digesting and clearing out.

Mullein:  Spiritually, mullein can help one to take a “breather” after much struggle and conflict. It will open the lungs and allow the life breath to flow in more easily, and allow toxins such as negative thoughts to be exhaled and released. It was worn in the past to invoke protection and it was said that if a plant was grown in the garden it would protect it as well.

the gift of passion, a renewed will to act, an exciting new beginning, a fresh encouragement to pursue one's heart' desire

The Ace of Wands represents the gift of passion, that spark of excitement and revigorating energy that inspires one's action. It speaks to a renewed sense of inner motivation to get up and do things with great enthusiasm.
In readings it signals a revigorated sense of energy to follow one's heart, a strong pull towards a new project, the inspired action that follows a sudden feeling of excitement towards a goal. It's the will and drive to get things done with passion and eagerness.

someone has set an intention to act, but hasn't made a move yet.The passion and will are there but a choice to take action needs to be made

TheTwo of Wands says there is a pull to move, but nothing has been set into motion yet as one is not so sure which direction to take, or whether they are ready to pursue their latest heart's desire. The world in his hand shows the abundance of opportunities available to him, one wand representing movement foward, expansion, whereas the other wand symbolizes inertia, staying in the comfort zone. In readings it signals the potential for growth that comes from courageously choosing to act on one's latest highest excitement, an invitation to progress by taking inspired action.

someone's plans have been put into action, good effort is made, waiting for result progress

The Three of Wands points to someone who has taken inspired action and is now contemplating the results of their efforts. It speaks to the idea of progress and expansion that comes from having decided to step out of one's comfort zone. In readings it signals potential for advancement, pondering on one's next move, further movement forward, looking far ahead into the future, aware of the potential obstacles, still choosing to expand.

holding on tight, clinging dearly to the material world, material stability, fear of losing

The Four of Wands represents someone who is about to celebrate an important and meaningful union, a soul connection, or any other form of success in the first stage of a project. It means your determination and actions have paid off and now it's time to celebrate. In a reading it signals a time to relax and enjoy, which marks a sense of victory after a period of great changes and rapid expansion. It also often points to the sense of joy and celebration involving the meeting of two souls that recognize each other in love.

conflict, aggression, inner struggle, a passionate disagreement, believing in different approaches

The Five of Wands represents someone who is experiencing some form of intense inner conflict. It is someone who is extremelly passionate about an approach, struggling with someone else in terms of how to act and behave towards a common goal. They might want the same thing, but strongly disagree with each other in terms of how to achieve it, which might lead to passionate disagreements, arguments and confrontation.
In readings it is an invitation to temper your impulses, to attempt to listen without resistence or insistence, to search for the middle ground, to practice respect, harmony, collaboration and support in relationships, and within yourself.

a sense of victory as if one's actions and efforts have paid off, leadership, success, recognition

The Six of Wands speaks of victory, success, public recognition and accomplishments. In readings it signals a great potential for achieving a much wanted positive result on something, a happy sign of things working out perfectly well, progress, achievement, victory, success, and social recognition. It feels as if one's actions and efforts have paid off.

defensiveness, protectiveness, standing upfor yourself, struggling to maintain the streak of success

The Seven of Wands represents someone who is struggling to maintain a streak of success and is feeling deffensive and like they need to prove they deserve their new title. It is a reminder that winning doesn't mean there won't ever be opposing views or challenges anymore. It takes groundedness to remain confident and centered. In readings, it reminds us to remain calm and to build the courage to carry on shinning, to hang in there and persevere in success.

fast communication, a strong flux of energy and determination to act, freedom, passion and space to move forward, travel

The Eight of Wands represents a strong flux of energy and determination to act. There's this sense of freedom, passion and space to move forward withone's individualplans. Intentions have been sent, and now thereis this sense of action in motion, of energy and desire to pursue one's goals. This is the energy of taking inspired action, of feeling revigorated and energertic and knowing exactly what to do. It's a fast moving energy that inspires and motivates. It can also bring good news, inspire fast communication, travel, or decision making.

feeling secure, financially stable, self-sufficient, whole, good enough, confident

The Nine of Wands represents someone who is feeling exhausted, like a wounded warrior, but keeps standing tall and strong even in the face of adversity. This is someone who is resilient and persevering, and keeps going no matter what, knowing giving up is not an option.
In readings it is an invitation to carry on, even if everyone and everything seems to be against you right now, for victory is right around the corner. It's that last pull to the finish line, a reminder of how far you've come, it says "don't give up now, you're almost there".

difficulty, utter exhaustion, burden, burning out, struggling to carry on, duty

The Ten of Wands represents the energy of someone who is experiencing increasing difficulty dealing with a situation. It feels like utter exaustion as one feels the duty to carry on under tremendous stress and burden. In readings it signals difficulty addressing a situation. It also suggests one might want to reconsider the effectiveness of investing time and energy on what doesn't seem to serve them anymore. If you are feeling overwhelmed and at the verge of a burn out, it could mean you have been mismanaging where you place your energy. What if you could let go of some of the excessive weight you're carrying?

The Page of Wands: is someone who is excited about experiencing something new or inspired to improve a skill. It's someone who's enthusiastic and full of renovated energy to pursue creative ideas. They're vigorous and passionate, optimistic and willing to explore. Somewhat impatient, hasty, spontaneous, childlike.

The Knight of Wands: is someone who's acting on their passion. Someone who moves fast, who is adventurous, energetic, charming and exciting. Someone going towards their goal, taking initiative. It's inspired action in motion. It's someone who is passionate, active, highly attractive and driven.
Queen of Wands: a feminine energy who is energetic, courageous, upbeat, and determined. Someone who is optimistic, confident, daring, and charismatic.

The King of Wands: is a masculine energy who is highly driven and proud. Someone who's living their life's passion to the fullest. Someone who is unstoppable, who is self-confident, enthusiastic and successful. One who has an entrepreneurial spirit, who is obsessed with life, who pushes himself to perfection, a charismatic leader with a great deal of vitality and motivation.

the gift of clarity, an important insight or having clarity on an issue, clear communication, a revigorated senseof focus,an honest adult conversation

The Ace of Swords represents the gift of clarity, wisdom and the inner harmony thatcomes from a mind that has access to the truth. In readings it signals the potential to reach a better understanding of an important issue, the receiving of a very much wanted message that clarifies things, or a clear and honest communication that lightens one's perception. It can also represent having an important insight that is life changing, a brilliant new idea and the revigorated sense of focus to plan and pursue it.

someone's utterly confused and unable to make a clear choice due to constant thoughts of doubt and uncertainty

The Two of Swords says someone's individual thoughts of worry or doubt are bringing confusion and uncertainty, therefore, they can't decide between unclear ideas. This card illustrates how our own distorted thoughts can cloud our minds and quickly temper the mental clarity of the Ace. The calm waters and moon in the back area are a reminder that we all have a source of guidance and to look within for clarity and wisdom. In readings it signals the potential to ground ourselves, take a few deep breaths and look deeper, listen to the subtle insights that spring from your intuition, the answers lie in silence.

someone is feeling deeply hurt by one's thoughts, words or actions

The Three of Swords is the card of heartbreak caused by someone's thoughts, words or actions. Although it is a card that speaks to being hurt (emotions, feelings), the fact it is a swords card tells us the pain could have been intensified by how the mind is perceiving the situation, by one's choice to recreate a hurtful scene in the mind, by distorted concepts, narratives and perceptions of self and other selves. In readings it signals the presence of a deep hurt that requires care, attention and healing, but also an invitation not to indulge in distorted mental narratives that are not helpful and perpetuate the pain.

meditation, inner peace, quieting thoughts, stability of the mind, self-care, healing, renovation

The Four of Swords represents someone who is in need of deep mental rest, healing, inner harmony and self-care. Someone's mind is in need of a pause after a period of exhaustion, which could be achieved through meditation, a good night sleep, getting a massage, therapy, some breathing exercise or even a break from work. In readings it signals an invitation or a period where one wants to take a step back from the chaos and allow room for some healing and self-care to take place.

mental conflict, mind cognitive distortions, unhealthy mental narratives and battle

The Five of Swords represents someone who wants to win a debate at all costs, either verbally or mentally, and thus, creates all sorts of mental narratives to justify their words and actions. Cognitive distortions such as mind reading: assuming what someone else is thinking without having much to go on; and catastrophizing: expecting the worst of someone or a situation; are usually taking place in the mind. Although all 5s represent conflict, this one is talking about what is happening in the mind, the narratives and concepts being created around a situation, how the intellect is trying to resolve an issue, mental and verbal communication based on distorted perceptions. In readings it signals an invitation to take a step back and ask yourself "Do you absolutely know what you're thinking or saying is true?" "Who would you be without that thought?"

moving on to calmer waters, leaving unhealthy mental narratives and useless arguments behind

The Six of Swords represents someone who is choosing to leave a turbulent situation behind. It speaks to the deliberate choice to get rid of unnecessary drama by refusing to engage in useless arguments, letting go of the urge to win debates, quitting unhealthy mental narratives that don't serveus anymore, while keeping only potential valuable lessons regarding a situation. In readings it shows someone who is deciding to move on to calmer waters, leaving distorted perceptions and useless arguments behind.

trickery, self deception, leaving something behind, plotting

The Seven of Swords represents someone who is attempting to be smart while leaving important bits of information out, which can lead to misunderstandings and a sense of deception. The original story of the card shows someone sneaking away from a military camp with five swords in his arms. His intentions are good, he wishes to avoid more conflict. However, the means could be too risky. This is someone who has not thought something through well enough, someone who just wants to escape, to get away, and by plotting in secret, risks being seen as trickery. In readings it is an invitation to ask yourself whether you are 100% sure your strategy includes all the important variables. What are you not considering? What are you leaving out? What are you running away from? What is the truth here?

self-doubt, self-criticism, victimization, unworthiness, self-judgment, negative self-talk

The Eight of Swords represents someone whose individual thoughts of self-doubt and self- criticism are becoming overwhelming and exhausting and making them feel stuck, like a victim, small or unworthy. The water in this card represents how our emotions are affected by our negative self-talk. There is no one else around symbolizing the fact that all these negative thoughts are one's individual creations, and don't necessarily reflect anyone else's opinion. The person is blindfolded representing the inability to see the truth, which is: we are all perfect, worthy, and divine exactly the way we are. We all fall sometimes, it's ok. You are alright. You are undeniably loved, be kind to yourself, reconnect with your inner light, free yourself.

feeling overwhelmed with anxiety, restless, worry, overthinking, panicking, stress, insomnia, excessively busy mind

The Nice of Swords represents someone whose excessive thinking is causing them to become anxious and insomniac. This is someone who's spent too much time worrying, catastrophizing, or ruminating, feeling trapped in unhealthy mental narratives that repeat and repeat. Too much time feeding negative thoughts might lead to depression and other mental health issues. It's time to let go of trying to change or control the past or the future with the mind. This card is an invitation to ask yourself whether that which is being remembered or feared is absolutely true, and even if it is, is it a useful thought? Who would I be without that thought? It's time to ground yourself, spend time in nature, do breath work, have some fun, watch a comedy, meditate, relax. Allow nature to take its course, remind yourself that "everything always works out for us", stay present, breathe.

reaching rock bottom, mental collapse, a sense of total defeat, like it's the end and there's no hope, utterly confused and unsettled, a sense of failure

The Ten of Swords represents someone who is stressing way too much over what they feel is the end of something. It symbolizes a sense of total defeat and failure where one's thoughts are going in circles recreating narratives of hopelessness and doom. In readings, it shows someone whose unsettling thoughts of loss and defeat make them feel like they've reached rock bottom. Someone's state of worry, exhaustion, and despair has reached a limit and is causing a sort of mental collapse. This card invites a shift in perception. While it is always wise to be kind to yourself and validate your feelings, choosing to remain stuck with an interpretation of something as a loss or a hurtful ending will only perpetuate the sense of disharmony. It isn't helpful and doesn't soothe the pain. Would you be willing to see this differently? What would if feel like to choose peace instead of this?

The Page of Swords: is someone who brings an exciting new insight or a delayed message. One bursting with new ideas, curious and eager to learn, an avid communicator who is willing and ready to share their thoughts. Somewhat flighty and anxious, but with an idea that might point to a new perspective or direction.

The Knight of Swords: is someone who is ambitious and acts quickly on their ideas. Someone who has a plan and is quick to make it happen. Someone who is intelligent and determined to succeed, a fast decision maker, someone assertive and sure of their own abilities. Someone who is coming fast with a message.
Queen of Swords: a feminine energy who is extremely intelligent and clear-minded. One who is straightforward and makes honest and reasonable decisions.

The King of Swords: is a masculine energy who is intelligent, wise, objective and level-headed. It's someone who is calm and collected, sensible and ethical. Someone who is clear-minded, a truthful leader, a strong communicator, a careful decision-maker. It's the wise judge or mediator, one who is impartial and just, one who is free of preconceived notions, and concerned with the truth.

the gift of stability,security, a new job, a raise, a promotion, a much-wanted gift or purchase, a proposal

The Ace of Pentacles represents the gift of stability in all material matters: health, work, relationships etc. Feeling safe. It offers a grounded sense of security in our physical life.
In readings it signals the potential to attract a much-wanted proposal, offer or gift, such as an offer of serious commitment in a relationship, a new business or career opportunity, being offered a raise or promotion, a new sense of health and renewal, or an opportunity to heal a physical issue.

someone may be juggling several projects at the moment and feeling overwhelmed

The Two of Pentacles says someone may be juggling several things at the moment and feeling overwhelmed with demands and commitments. There's this feeling of having too many resources to manage and not knowing how to deal with all of it. It might illustrate someone wanting to have their cake and eat it too. The choppy waters in the background represent the emotional instability that comes from trying to manage too much at once. In readings it signals an invitation to reflect upon how sustainable it is to attempt to manage multiple options at once. It might mean a choice has to be made before one finds emotional balance again.

someone's work is being recognized, being sought for partnership, collaboration, receiving support

The Three of Pentacles represents being recognized for your efforts and talents. It speaks to the idea of partnership where one receives all the support and resources necessary to share their gifts with the world. In readings it signals the presence of a supportive energy, an opportunity to collaborate with others, a potential partnership, working with a team towards a common goal.

a soulful love connection, stability in a commitment, party, a gathering to celebrate an important event

The Four of Pentacles represents someone who has reached a certain level of stability in their career or in a relationship, or has achieved an important goal, but is now afraid to lose it and is holding on tightly to what they've got.
In readings it is a reminder that although it is ok to save for a rainy day, it is important to trust your divine right to be stable and prosper. The more we hold on to things with fear, the more we block our own flow of abundance, love, health and wealth. Relax. Trust.

lack, scarcity, feeling out in the cold, abandonment, rejection, missing someone, health issues

The Five of Pentacles represents someone who is missing something in the material world. It is someone who is either dealing with financial difficulties or is feeling a loss, abandomnent or rejection in a relationship. It might also represent someone dealing with some sort of health issue. Either way, one's sense of security is negatively affected here, but the temple window in this card represents how there is always divine assistance available and at reach. In readings it is an invitation to look around and connect with the abundance of protection, love and resources still around. Count your blessings, rest, trust that everything always works out.

attracting a relationship or situation where there is equal give and take, generosity, receptivity

The Six of pentacles speaks of balance in relationships, of the ability to intuitively know when it's time to give, while also being open to receive. It speaks of both generosity and receptivity. In readings it signals the potential to attract a relationship or situation where there is equal give and take.

perseverance, impatience, long-term success, sustainable results, investment, reflection, planning

The Seven of Pentacles represents someone who has been working really hard while making very slow progress. It speaks to the planning stages of a project where there is some investment, but results might not be showing up yet. It is about rewards, harvest, results after hard work, and trust in the process. In readings it is a reminder to persevere and trust that long-term success comes with diligence and patience.

putting in work, dedication, diligence, discipline, effort, willingness, consistence

The Eight of Pentacles represents someone who is putting in (or being invited to put in) work and dedication to better themselves, their career, their relationship or their physical health. This is someone who is patient and determined and understands the nature of time and the role of consistence, someone who is a master of self-discipline and takes joy in perfecting themselves through their work, the adoption of healthy daily habits and behavior, or further education. One whoperseveres with diligence and patience.

holding on, persisting, obstination, resilience, wounded but strong, inner strength, fatigue, close to success

The Nine of Pentacles represents someone who is is feeling absolutely abundant, independent and prosper. This is someone who knows their worth, who understands their own value, who is entirely connected to the abundance of resources around them and knows how to multiply them. Someone who is self-fulfilled and in touch with the infinite possibilities in life.
In readings it shows someone who is feeling secure and successful, stable and confident, ready to reap the fruits of their sense of self-worth.

reaching one 's be-all and end-all of all matters material: a comfortable healthy body, the dream house, a stable relationship, financial stability, a great career

The Ten of Pentacles represents manifesting the reality of one's dreams in the physical world. It is about getting the degree you've always wanted, it's buying the house of your dreams, it is the good feeling healthy body, the money flowing consistently, the relationship stability in the form of a commitment or a marriage, it's the successful career, and whatever one finds in their heart to describe their highest material aspiration at a given moment. In readings it is a really positive sign and represents someone who is, due to a feeling of utter spiritual abundance, manifesting prosperity, security, loving and stable connections, success, and infinite resources. It' s the be-all and end-all ideal in material life.

The Page of Pentacles is someone who recognizes an opportunity and is willing and ready to nurture it to success. It is someone who comes with an offer to lay the groundwork to achieve success. It is someone who feels hopeful, one who is practical and ambitious, somewhat insecure and inexperienced, but loyal and patient.

The Knight of Pentacles is someone who is coming with a tangible offer in business or love. Someone who is responsible, stable, reliable, and patient. Someone who doesn't act quickly, but makes solid well-thought responsible moves. Someone who is thinking long-term, who is dedicated and grounded.
Queen of Pentacles: a feminine energy who is extremely generous and nurturing. One who is abundant, grounded, healthy, positive, wealthy and self-sufficient.

The King of Pentacles is a masculine energy who is successful, ambitious, grounded and mature. It's someone who is a good provider, who is prosperous, wealthy and supportive. It's someone who is a confident leader, who is warm and generous, and yet firm and determined. It's someone who has understood the laws of abundance and prosperity, and is willing to share and multiply.

the gift of love, a new beginning in love, an offer that brings emotional fulfilment, an opportunity to rekindle a relationship.

The Ace of Cups represents the gift of love and all the things that fill one's heart with joy and warmth. It speaks to a renewed sense of emotional fulfilment, the feeling of well-being and elation whereonejust can'tstopsmiling. In readings it signals the potential to attract a new love interest, or an opportunity to start all over again in an important relationship. It also represents potential to develop a deep friendly connection with someone, or simply a revigorated feeling of true love and ease.

someone has decided to form an emotional bond that is profound and meaningful

The Two of Cups says someone is choosing to invest on a deep loving relationship. Such choice can show up in the form of a proposal, a commitment, or merely the recognition of a strong spiritual connection between a couple, friends or familymembers. They hold their Cups at equal height symbolising equality and acceptance within the relationship, balancing the energies of give and take. In readings it signals a decision has been made on both sides to exchange loving energies with each other. It's the card of union, commitment, soul mates, connection, harmony, acceptance, inclusion and affinity.

someone is about to experience and share immense joy, celebrating love, warm feelings, connection

The Three of Cups speaks to someone who is getting ready to celebrate and share their joy with loved ones. It is a card of connection, of deep loving bonds, of feeling joy and warm feelings for others, happy social relationships, announcing an achievement, sharing a success story, partying! In readings it signals potential for enjoyment and happy times, a joyful gathering with loved ones, celebrating an important accomplishment with friends and family, connecting, sharing immense joy with others, fun and laughter, feeling good and at home with others.

disappointment, emotional detachment, lack of appreciation, apathy, boredom

The Four of Cups speaks to someone who is feeling disappointed or bored, struggling to appreciate how gifted they are and the opportunities that keep showing up for them. Although it is clear that there is enough source of emotional stability and support all around, someone here can't feel it. In readings it's an invitation to reflect upon what you really want, to remain open to infinite possibilities and to allow for things to unfold for your highest good without unnecessary insistence. It's an invitation to get into the receptive mode by deliberately noticing what's going right in life.

emotional loss, sadness, depression, grief, delusion, self pity, a broken heart, despair

The Five of Cups represents feeling the loss of someone or something that used to provide emotional support. It speaks to feelings of grief, sadness, self-pity, depression, despair as one seems to be focusing too much on what's gone, feeling like there is no hope left. However, right behind them, there are two cups sitting upright, representing the love and emotional support that remains there. In a reading it is a reminder that, although it is essential that we validate our feelings with kindness and compassion, it is equally important to be able to look around and deliberately recognize the love, support and connections that have never departed from us, as well as understand that well- being abounds in the universe and that nothing is ever truly lost.

feeling nostalgic, dealing with an important soul connection, inner child work

The Six of Cups represents a sort of reconnection with one's past. It brings nostalgic feelings of warmth and safety as one recognizes the presence of a very loving familiar energy. In a reading it signals the potential for reuniting with a deep soul connection. It could also show up as an invitation to do inner child work where one chooses to parent their inner child by giving themselves the love they might be seeking externally.

feeling overwhelmed with too many options, illusions, confusion, multiple choices, fantasy, dream

The Seven of Cups represents someone who is finding it hard to choose between a great deal of opportunities available. Although it speaks to dreams, wishes, and having multiple choices, one canfeel overwhelmed having too many options to choose from, and the confusion might lead to illusions, indecision, fantasy, and ungroundedness. In readings it signals an abundance of opportunities available to you, with an invitation to ground yourself, maybe connect with your heart center and ask: Which option feels true?What's my highest excitement right now? Which option leads to my greatest joy? Which path is aligned with my highest good at the moment?

emotional disconnect, walking away, letting go, searching for truth, leaving behind

The Eight of Cups represents someone has decided to disconnect from someone else, a place, or a situation they care deeply about in order to go after their wish fulfillment. This is someone who is willing (or being invited) to let go of something really meaninful to them - which might not be working anymore - in order to pursue something bigger. It involves having the courage to leave behind something that was once gained and taking a solitary journey towards the light within the self. It is really a journey to self-love, the path to self liberation, the looking for love in the right places, the realignment with one's inner strength, a path to self-discovery and of loving the real YOU who is found.

feeling emotionally fulfilled, huge contentment, inner peace, glow, joy

The Nine of Cups represents someone who has found true love and joy within themselves, one whose highest wishes have been fulfilled as a consequence of this realization. This is someone who feels at the top of their game, experiencing a sense of utter bliss, self-acceptance, worth and wholeness within. This is individual dreams coming true, it's having everything you need on an emotional level, feeling limitless, deeply content, fulfilled and radiant. It shows up as a profound love and appreciation for the self and life. It means happiness, inner peace and triumph in both the spiritual and temporal spheres. In readings it signals reaching a sense of absolute elation, utter inner joy, and personal satisfaction in all areas of life.

The Ten of Cups represents the energy of someone
whose heart is full of joy, happiness, love, and a
sense of connection. This is someone who feels ready
to experience a happy, blissful, and harmonious
relationship with a partner. Someone who's already
found joy within themselves and is ready to share
that joy. This is one of the most positive cards in the
tarot and speaks to the idea that when you are in
harmony with yourself, you experience harmonious
relationships. In reading it signals the potential to
have all your emotional needs met within a
connection, to share a life of true bliss and love with
